highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable Opus model featuring a 1M token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is a significant upgrade for developers working on large codebases or long-running agentic tasks in Claude Code. If you use Claude Code, Opus 5 is now the default Opus model automatically.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Opus 5 Default, Strict Network Sandbox, and DirectoryAdded Hook
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.219 adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model in Claude Code and introduces a new `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that silently blocks any non-allowlisted hosts in sandboxed commands — great for security-conscious teams. A new `DirectoryAdded` hook also gives developers more control over automating actions when directories are added to the workspace.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command has been updated to run as a background subagent, meaning it no longer clutters your main conversation thread with review output. This keeps your chat focused and ensures stacked slash commands correctly target the right code for review. This is a quality-of-life improvement that makes code review workflows much cleaner.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216: Filesystem Sandbox Toggle and Quadratic Slowdown Fix
highlights.summary: A new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting lets you skip filesystem isolation while still controlling network egress, giving teams more granular sandbox control. More importantly, a major performance bug was fixed where long sessions experienced multi-second stalls due to message normalization growing quadratically with the number of turns. If you've noticed Claude Code getting sluggish in long sessions, upgrading to this version should help significantly.

highlights.title: Claude Code Has a Hardcoded Instruction Telling Opus 5 Not to Use Subagents
highlights.summary: A Reddit post on HN has surfaced that Claude Code contains a hardcoded system prompt instructing Opus 5 to avoid spawning subagents, which may limit its agentic capabilities in certain workflows. This is a useful finding for advanced users who rely on multi-agent orchestration and want to understand why Opus 5 may behave differently than expected. It's worth following the thread for any official Anthropic response or workaround.

highlights.title: Show HN: A Local Merge Queue for Parallel Claude Code Agents
highlights.summary: A developer running 4-5 parallel Claude Code agents pushing up to 90 commits a day on a MacBook Air built a local merge queue to prevent agents from colliding on builds, tests, and dev servers. The tool helps manage resource contention on low-memory machines without burning CI minutes on every push. If you're experimenting with parallel agents, this open-source project is a practical solution to a real bottleneck.

highlights.title: Get EVERYTHING Out of Claude Code in 13 Minutes (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This fast-paced YouTube tutorial promises to take you from beginner to proficient Claude Code user in just 13 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a quick but comprehensive overview. It covers core features and practical workflows so you can start being productive immediately. A great starting point if you're new to Claude Code or want a structured refresher.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: This 30-minute YouTube tutorial offers a focused deep-dive into Claude Code for developers who want to move beyond the basics and build real mastery of the tool. It's structured to be time-efficient while still covering intermediate techniques that improve daily workflow. A solid choice for developers who have the basics down and want to level up quickly.

tips_of_the_day: If your Claude Code sessions feel sluggish after many turns, upgrade to v2.1.216 or later — a quadratic performance bug in long sessions has been fixed and you should notice much snappier responses.
Use the `/code-review` command without worrying about polluting your conversation: as of v2.1.218 it runs as a background subagent, so your main chat stays clean and focused on your current task.

When running multiple parallel Claude Code agents on a single machine, avoid letting them all trigger builds and dev servers simultaneously — consider a local merge queue or staggered task scheduling to prevent resource exhaustion and forced restarts.
